articles.title: Read the workspace overview
articles.summary: Use the overview to decide which product needs attention before starting daily work.
articles.before: Sign in to the correct Hub workspace. Allow the app summaries to finish loading.
steps: Check the workspace name at the top and the account name at the right. Confirm that you are working in the intended organisation.
Read Today’s Focus and Needs your attention. Open the relevant source app from its card or the attention item.
Read the period printed beside each metric. POS sales use the last 30 days; finance and other summaries can use different periods.
Use Refresh Hub data or Refresh dashboard when the displayed information needs updating. Then check each product’s reported date.
articles.check: A completed summary shows the reporting sources and their dates. An em dash, Unknown or Awaiting data means the value is unavailable.
articles.note: Dashboard summaries are not service-uptime or security certificates. Check each source and reporting date.
articles.tags: dashboard metrics unknown em dash data refresh overview figures

articles.title: Launch and return between apps
articles.summary: Open the correct app with the account and workspace information supplied by Hub.
articles.before: You need an assigned app and a valid signed-in Hub session.
steps: Select My Apps. Read the How sign-in works panel before choosing a product.
Select Launch on Tiquet, FFPRO, Marketing or POS. Let the secure launch finish before deciding that access has failed.
For Academy, use its separate learner account. CombatZone opens its own public booking experience.
Use Back to Vision79 Hub or Back to Hub inside the product when you need the launcher again. If a direct product bookmark returns you to Hub, launch the product again from My Apps.
articles.check: The destination shows the expected product name and the correct workspace. A loading screen alone does not confirm successful access.
articles.note: App access is determined by account role and assigned modules. A link being visible does not mean every operation is permitted.
articles.tags: login sign in access launch app loading stuck return bookmark

articles.title: Invite a team member
articles.route: Hub > Team & Access > Invite Team Member
articles.summary: Prepare a staff invitation with the correct role and explicitly selected applications.
articles.before: Use an account allowed to manage team access. Confirm the recipient’s email address and required duties.
steps: Open Team & Access and select Invite Team Member or New invitation. This requires permission to manage team access.
Enter the intended email address. Choose Manager, Staff or Viewer after reading the role description.
Select only the assigned apps that the person needs.
Review the email, role and apps, then choose Create invitation. Check the saved invitation and its expiry.
articles.check: The invitation appears in Team invitations. Creating an invitation does not mean it has been accepted.
articles.note: Only selected apps appear for that member. FFPRO access is isolated to the member’s identity and explicitly shared projects. Check current app choices and invitation expiry on screen.
articles.tags: invite colleague employee team staff add user role permissions access

articles.title: Check account security
articles.summary: Confirm the account’s two-factor authentication status and understand workspace access.
articles.before: Open Security while signed in as the account you intend to review.
steps: Wait for the Security screen to load, then read Two-factor authentication for your own account.
Review the Authenticator app panel and follow the account’s current security requirements.
Read Workspace permissions. App access follows role and assigned modules; finance visibility is more restricted.
Sign out on shared devices. If the account or MFA status is unexpected, ask your authorised administrator to investigate.
articles.check: Your own account displays its expected security status.
articles.note: Never share authenticator secrets, MFA codes or recovery codes in chat or screenshots.
articles.tags: mfa 2fa two factor authenticator account security password recovery

articles.title: Review billing and plan access
articles.summary: Read the workspace plan, included apps and saved billing records before requesting a change.
articles.before: You need billing visibility for the intended workspace.
steps: Open Billing. Read Current plan, Plan status, Renewal and Enabled V79 apps.
Review the package and app choices before requesting a subscription. Check billing period, app allowances, staff capacity, supplements and any setup charge.
Use Refresh saved requests or Refresh invoice history when you need the latest saved records. Check each record’s own currency and status.
For a customer payment, follow the official instructions shown for that workspace and wait for verified payment confirmation before expecting access to change.
articles.check: The saved billing record and the workspace entitlement agree. A browser redirect or a bank-transfer claim alone does not activate access.
articles.note: Follow the workspace’s current official payment instructions. Sandbox transactions are tests and do not establish paid access. A display currency label does not convert an invoice’s stored currency.
articles.tags: billing plan subscription upgrade renewal payment paid invoice sandbox currency pricing cost

articles.title: Triage the service workload
articles.summary: Find overdue, unassigned and high-priority service work quickly.
articles.before: Launch Tiquet from Hub and confirm the active workspace.
steps: Read Active jobs and Overdue jobs. Compare Outstanding invoices with Cash collected; they describe different things.
Work through Attention Required. Select a job title to inspect its owner, due date, scope and stage.
Use Pipeline Distribution to see where work is accumulating, then open Jobs Pipeline for the full list.
Review Recent Activity before making a change so you understand the latest action and who recorded it.
articles.check: Every urgent job has an understood next step, responsible person and realistic service date.
articles.note: Cash collected is based on the confirmed payment ledger. A completed job is not automatically a settled invoice.
articles.tags: dashboard overdue unassigned workload priority

articles.title: Create and maintain client records
articles.summary: Create a client once and reuse that record for service requests.
articles.before: Have the client’s approved contact details. Search for an existing record first.
steps: Open Clients and search by name, company or email to avoid duplicates.
Select Add Client. Enter Full Name, Company, Email Address and Phone Number.
Choose Industry if an appropriate category exists, then enter the Address. Check spelling, country code and contact ownership.
Select Create Client, then find the saved record. Use Edit Client for later corrections and confirm the revised details remain visible.
articles.check: The client appears in Client Management and is available in the New Request client selector.
articles.note: Industry choices are managed in Settings. Use a fictional example during training, such as Example Services Ltd, and avoid sending welcome emails or broadcasts unless that action is intended.
articles.tags: add create client customer company contact industry edit

articles.title: Create a new service request
articles.summary: Capture the requested outcome, customer, priority, owner and deadline in one job.
articles.before: The client should already exist. Confirm the scope and urgency with the requester.
steps: Enter a clear Job Title and select the correct Client. For example, “Investigate intermittent office Wi-Fi”.
Choose Low, Medium or High priority based on business impact. Add Estimated Budget only when you have a supported estimate.
Choose Assigned To and a Due Date. Use Job Description to record the problem, location, impact and the agreed next step.
Select Submit Request. Return to Jobs Pipeline and search the title to confirm the new job.
articles.check: The job appears in Incoming Request with the expected client, priority, assignee and due date.
articles.note: A useful description states what is happening, who is affected, when it began and what success looks like. Do not put passwords or sensitive access credentials in the job.
articles.tags: create new ticket job request assign due date budget description

articles.title: Find jobs and move them through the pipeline
articles.summary: Keep the service stage aligned with the actual work completed.
articles.before: Read the job’s current scope and activity before changing its stage.
steps: Use the title/client search, priority filter and assignee filter to narrow the workload. Choose List for tabular detail or Board for stages.
Open the intended job card. Confirm the client, owner, due date and required action.
On Board, use Advance or the back control when the real service milestone has been reached. The inspected sequence is Incoming Request, Estimation, In Progress, Review, Invoiced, Completed and Paid.
Reopen the job and inspect its stage and activity log. Review the invoice and payment ledger before expecting a job to reach Paid.
articles.check: The updated stage matches the evidence of work, and any payment-related transition is supported by recorded payments.
articles.note: The board scrolls horizontally to later stages. Moving a card changes the record; opening a card or switching List/Board only changes your view.
articles.tags: pipeline stage move advance paid completed board list search filter

articles.title: Update job details and internal notes
articles.summary: Keep the job’s operational record useful to the next team member.
articles.before: Open the exact job. Confirm that the title and client match the work you intend to update.
steps: Review the summary, Assigned To, Tags and Description. Check the due date and the job value before relying on them.
Record a concise Job Note describing the action, outcome and next step. Use the adjacent add control, then check that the note appears.
For an internal planning brief, use Internal reply drafts and Save draft only. Read the on-screen statement that no customer message or email is sent.
Review Activity Log after an update and reopen the job if needed to confirm that the saved information remains.
articles.check: The correct job shows the intended note or internal draft. An internal draft remains separate from customer-visible communication.
articles.note: Example note: “Checked access-point power and uplink. Issue remains on the first floor. Next: review radio settings with the engineer tomorrow.” Avoid vague entries such as “done”.
articles.tags: note save notes job tags description draft activity log edit

articles.title: Prepare documents and review invoice exposure
articles.route: Tiquet > Open job > Automated Business Documents; Invoices
articles.summary: Prepare a job document and check the difference between invoicing and money received.
articles.before: Check the business profile, currency, tax defaults and payment terms before generating a document.
steps: Open the job and locate Automated Business Documents. Choose ESTIMATE, WORK ORDER or INVOICE for the intended purpose.
Review the generated document against the client, scope, price, tax and terms before sharing it.
Open Invoices. Search for the relevant job or client and compare Invoice value, Received, Outstanding and Status.
Check recorded payment evidence before treating the invoice as settled. The interface requires payments to cover the job value before it becomes Paid.
articles.check: The document is correct, and the ledger supports the displayed payment status. No invoice should be treated as cash received solely because it was generated.
articles.note: If the payment ledger cannot load, use Retry and contact support if the issue persists. Unavailable does not mean zero. The manual does not verify the final payment-entry controls.
articles.tags: invoice estimate work order payment outstanding received settled paid ledger retry document

articles.title: Store files and use the payroll tracker
articles.summary: Maintain project assets and internal compensation records.
articles.before: Have the correct file or approved employee details ready. Payroll records require authorised staff access.
steps: In Files, use Upload Files to select the intended asset. Search the repository afterwards and verify that the correct filename is present.
In Payroll Tracker, choose Employees to review roles, compensation type, rate, payment method and status.
Use Add Employee for a new authorised record. Review details before generating Payroll Records.
Check the period and the employee list before Generate Payroll Records. Use the records tab to verify the saved result and internal payment status.
articles.check: The intended file or payroll record is visible and belongs to the correct workspace and period.
articles.note: Tiquet states that it does not transfer payroll funds or calculate statutory deductions. A tracked payment status must be reconciled with the actual payment made outside the app.
articles.tags: upload file payroll employee wages salary statutory deductions funds

articles.title: Configure service business defaults
articles.summary: Set the details used by client records, generated documents and broadcasts.
articles.before: Only change approved business details. Some controls, such as logo upload, take effect immediately.
steps: Review Business Profile: name, email, phone, website and address. The logo accepts PNG, JPEG, WEBP or GIF up to 5 MB.
Set Invoice Defaults, including Currency, Default tax rate and Default payment terms. Use the business’s approved figures.
Maintain Industries and review Welcome Email and Newsletter templates. Use plain text as instructed by the screen.
Choose Save Settings after reviewing changes. For a newsletter, separately check the selected opted-in audience before using Broadcast.
articles.check: Reopen Settings and confirm the saved defaults. Preview a generated document before relying on the changes.
articles.note: Broadcast sends customer email and needs its own deliberate review. Users & Roles can be unavailable when Hub ownership verification fails; use the displayed Retry verification and escalate rather than bypassing Hub access.
articles.tags: settings logo invoice tax currency industry newsletter welcome email broadcast users roles verification

articles.title: Understand the commerce dashboard
articles.summary: Review sales, refunds, gross profit and incoming stock in one place.
articles.before: Launch POS from Hub and check the workspace role and currency.
steps: Read Net revenue, Completed sales, Average sale and Gross profit with their reporting periods.
Remember that net revenue is after refunds, while gross profit is before operating expenses. Read each label rather than assuming all cards use the same definition.
Open Recent sales or View all to inspect transactions. Use Review stock signals for supply concerns.
Open Purchasing for incoming orders and Inventory for current balances. Use Refresh when the screen needs an updated snapshot.
articles.check: The dashboard figures can be traced to sales or stock records in the same workspace.
articles.note: The documented POS currency is XCD (EC$). Check the current currency label. Refunds can make the original sale total differ from net revenue.
articles.tags: dashboard revenue gross profit refunds overview currency

articles.title: Add a product or service
articles.summary: Create a catalogue item with the correct selling price, cost and stock behaviour.
articles.before: Prepare a unique SKU, product category, approved price, cost and tax rate.
steps: Enter Product name, SKU and Category. Use a name staff can recognise at the register.
Enter Selling price (XCD), Unit cost (XCD) and Tax rate (%). Check decimal places and whether your business’s price includes any expected tax treatment.
Choose Product type: Stocked product, Service or Non-stock item. Check Track stock only when quantity control is intended.
Select Create product. Verify the product, variant, SKU and price in the catalogue, then check its register availability.
articles.check: The item appears under Products with the correct price and stock-tracking behaviour.
articles.note: Creating the product does not establish the physical opening balance. Use a supported inventory movement or receipt to record stock; do not invent quantities to make the register available.
articles.tags: create add product service sku barcode price cost tax track stock catalogue

articles.title: Open the register and prepare a sale
articles.summary: Start the correct till session with a physically counted cash float.
articles.before: Have the authorised register selected and the opening cash counted.
steps: Open Register and confirm the intended register and location.
If the register is closed, choose Open register. Enter Opening cash float (XCD) using the cash actually present.
Review the amount before submitting Open register. Confirm that the closed-register warning clears.
Search the Catalogue by name, SKU or barcode. Select the correct product and check Current sale before proceeding to payment.
articles.check: The register is open and the current sale contains the intended items and quantities.
articles.note: Opening a till records an operational cash session. Only open the register when authorised to begin that cash session.
articles.tags: open register till closed cash float search barcode sale

articles.title: Check a sale before taking payment
articles.summary: Review the basket and server-calculated payment total before charging the customer.
articles.before: Use an open register. Confirm stock availability and the selected product/variant.
steps: Search for each item and add it to Current sale. Verify the quantities and remove any accidental selection before continuing.
Check Subtotal, Estimated tax and Total. The screen states that final pricing and tax are calculated by the server at checkout.
Select Charge for the intended basket, then review the payment details and final total shown on the next screen before confirming.
After an authorised payment, verify the saved sale in Sales and reconcile the payment record with the money or external terminal result.
articles.check: A completed sale has a saved transaction record and matching payment evidence. A clicked Charge button alone is not a completed sale.
articles.note: The manual documents the basket and Charge controls. Exact final payment-confirmation and register-closing controls require a verified walkthrough; follow the current screen or ask support.
articles.tags: checkout charge sale basket payment total tax price confirm receipt

articles.title: Create quotes, orders, invoices and layaway
articles.summary: Record an order with the correct commercial type, item and payment dates.
articles.before: Have the product, location, quantity and agreed terms ready.
steps: Choose Location and optionally Customer. Walk-in customer is available when no named customer is selected.
Choose Order type: Quote, Order, Invoice or Layaway. Select Product and enter Quantity.
Enter any Line discount (XCD), Deposit required, Valid until, Payment due and Notes. Confirm that the amount is an approved discount, not an accidental price reduction.
Select Create order, then open the saved order and check its type, amount, dates and status.
articles.check: The intended order appears in Customer orders with the correct commercial terms.
articles.note: A required deposit is a term on the order; it does not prove payment has been received. Quotes and orders should not be reported as completed sales without the relevant fulfilment and payment evidence.
articles.tags: quote order invoice layaway deposit discount due date

articles.title: Review sales and process an authorised return
articles.summary: Record the correct return quantity and stock disposition against the original sale.
articles.before: Find the original transaction and confirm the customer’s return is authorised.
steps: In Sales, open Return / refund for the intended sale. Confirm the transaction identifier and original item.
Select the Item and Quantity to return. Check any previous returns; the server validates them before posting stock or money.
Choose whether to Return to sellable stock. Select Refund method and enter the external refund reference for a non-cash refund, plus a clear Return reason.
Review all details before Complete return. Then verify the sale’s revised status, refund record and any returned inventory.
articles.check: The refund and stock movement agree with the authorised return and actual refund payment.
articles.note: The documented methods are Cash, External card terminal, Bank transfer and Mobile wallet. Damaged or unusable goods should not return to sellable stock. Recording a refund reference does not itself transfer money.
articles.tags: refund return damaged sellable sale quantity payment cash card transfer wallet

articles.title: Record a stock adjustment
articles.summary: Record a justified change to stock without confusing it with a sale or supplier order.
articles.before: Count the affected goods and identify the correct location and SKU.
steps: Review Inventory first, including On hand and Available quantities.
Open Adjust stock. Choose Location, Product and Movement: Add stock, Remove stock, Damage or Expired.
Enter a positive Quantity for the selected movement and a specific Reason. Check the movement direction before committing.
Choose Record adjustment and verify the revised balance at the intended location.
articles.check: The stock balance changes in the expected direction and by the supported quantity.
articles.note: Example: record 2 units as Damage after confirming they are unusable. Avoid entering a negative quantity and a removal movement together. A clear reason helps the owner reconcile stock later.
articles.tags: adjust inventory damage expired add remove stock quantity reason

articles.title: Use cycle counts and stock transfers
articles.summary: Reconcile counted stock and move inventory between assigned locations.
articles.before: Use a controlled count period and identify the source/destination locations for a transfer.
steps: Choose Cycle count when you need to compare physical quantities with the stock record. Count the selected items before posting variances.
Review count differences with the responsible person. Confirm approved corrections rather than automatically accepting every discrepancy.
Choose Transfer stock for movement between locations. Confirm the product, quantity and the correct destination.
Inspect the saved cycle count or transfer afterwards and check the affected Inventory balances.
articles.check: The stock-control record explains why the balances changed, and the physical movement agrees with the system.
articles.note: The manual does not verify later approval/posting screens. Follow the current controls and ask an authorised supervisor before posting an unfamiliar stock correction.
articles.tags: cycle count transfer stock locations variance reconcile

articles.title: Prepare suppliers and purchase orders
articles.summary: Set up supply relationships before creating a draft order.
articles.before: Have supplier details, a product SKU, delivery location, quantity and expected delivery date ready.
steps: Use Add supplier to prepare the supplier record. Then use Link supplier product to establish which product that supplier provides.
Choose Purchase order. Select Supplier, Delivery location and Product.
Enter Order quantity, Expected delivery and Notes. Verify that the product is linked to the chosen supplier.
Select Create draft order and review the saved draft before sending or progressing it through any later purchasing process.
articles.check: A draft purchase order exists with the correct supplier, item, quantity and delivery location.
articles.note: A purchase order is separate from stock receipt and supplier payment. The manual does not verify downstream receiving controls.
articles.tags: supplier purchase order draft po receiving receipt incoming stock

articles.title: Set a replenishment policy
articles.summary: Create stock-planning inputs that match real demand and supplier lead time.
articles.before: Use a linked supplier/product where appropriate and confirm normal demand and supply delays.
steps: Choose Location and Product, then the Preferred supplier if it is available in linked products.
Set Safety stock units, Review period (days) and Planning lead time (days). Use a Daily demand override only when you can justify it.
Select Save policy, then use Recalculate from Smart replenishment.
Review recommendations before Create draft POs. Check quantities, supplier constraints and cash availability before progressing any resulting order.
articles.check: The recommendation can be explained by the saved policy and current stock/demand information.
articles.note: Choose review periods and lead times for your business. Caribbean import delays and supplier reliability should inform the actual settings.
articles.tags: reorder replenishment safety stock lead time demand policy draft purchase

articles.title: Review money and understand the figures
articles.summary: Review cash, commitments and objectives before recording or planning financial activity.
articles.before: Use your own FFPRO identity or an explicitly shared project. Check display currency.
steps: Read Net Worth, Cash Available, Monthly Cashflow and Daily spending guide with their definitions.
Review Projects & Planner Summary, Schedule & Calendar Highlights and Financial Objectives Progress.
Use Overview for a summary and Analysis for detailed records, budgets and spending views.
Use the Hide amounts control before screen-sharing, then verify visually that sensitive values are masked.
articles.check: You understand the source and period of the values you intend to use. A spending guide is an estimate, particularly before unpaid commitments.
articles.note: Switching the display currency changes labels; the interface explicitly states that it does not convert stored amounts. Check transaction currency and account data before comparing figures.
articles.tags: money net worth cash available monthly cashflow daily spending hide amounts currency conversion

articles.title: Record an expense, income or transfer
articles.summary: Save a transaction with the correct type, account, date and category.
articles.before: Have the original receipt or transaction evidence. Check whether the entry already exists.
steps: Select EXPENSE, INCOME or TRANSFER at the top of the Transaction form.
Enter Amount and select Payment source. Check the displayed currency and the account that actually received or spent the money.
Set Date, Category and Description. TODAY and YESTERDAY help with recent entries, but confirm the final date.
Review the complete entry before CONFIRM ENTRY. Return to Analysis and locate the transaction to check that it saved once.
articles.check: The ledger has one accurate entry and the expected account/category impact. A transfer should not be mistaken for new operating income.
articles.note: Example description: “Office router replacement, supplier invoice 1042”. Record the real amount once; adding it manually and then importing the same statement can create duplicates.
articles.tags: add record transaction expense income transfer category account date duplicates ledger

articles.title: Capture receipts and review statement imports
articles.route: FFPRO > Money > Review-first capture or Import Statement
articles.summary: Turn source documents into reviewed ledger candidates.
articles.before: Prepare a readable receipt or PDF/CSV statement. Check the account and date range you intend to import.
steps: Use Import Statement or the upload control in Review-first capture to choose the intended document.
For typed capture, describe the transaction clearly, including amount, date and purpose. Use the manual form if the interpretation is uncertain.
Read every extracted candidate against the original source. Correct amounts, date, description, category and account; check for duplicates.
Approve only the entries you intend to add. Verify the resulting ledger after import and retain the original source for reconciliation.
articles.check: Only approved, checked entries appear in the ledger. The screen states that imports remain outside the ledger until approval.
articles.note: Review extraction against the source. The manual does not verify extraction accuracy or the exact final approval controls; ask support if these differ from the screen.
articles.tags: import upload receipt statement csv pdf voice capture extract approval duplicates

articles.title: Analyse spending and control category budgets
articles.summary: Compare periods and trace unusual amounts back to transactions.
articles.before: Make sure transactions and account balances are current enough for the question you are asking.
steps: Choose the reporting Period: Week, Month, Year or Custom. Set Compare to Prior Period, Prior Year or None.
Switch between Overview, Spending, Cashflow and More views. Check the displayed range before reading a variance.
In Category Spend Matrix & Budget Control, sort by spending, variance, budget usage or transaction volume. Use Drill into transactions to inspect the underlying entries.
Use Edit budget limit for an approved category limit, then verify the saved value and progress indicator.
articles.check: The transaction list, selected range and budget explain the conclusion you draw.
articles.note: If generated wording uses a different currency label, reconcile with the ledger currency and original amounts before relying on it.
articles.tags: analysis budget limit spending period compare variance categories drill transactions

articles.title: Manage recurring bills and income
articles.summary: Keep planned commitments and expected income visible.
articles.before: Know the amount, category and next expected date. Verify that a similar commitment does not already exist.
steps: Open the settings gear and select RECURRING. Review existing Fixed expenses and Recurring inflows.
Under Register new recurring bill, enter the description, amount, category and date. Review before AUTHORIZE COMMITMENT.
For income, use Register recurring income with the expected next receipt date and choose REGISTER INFLOW.
Use the edit control for corrections. Check that the saved amount and next date appear correctly in Settings and relevant finance views.
articles.check: The intended commitment or inflow appears once with the correct amount and due date.
articles.note: A recurring commitment is a plan. It does not establish that a bill has been paid, and an expected inflow is not confirmed cash. Reconcile actual receipts and payments separately.
articles.tags: recurring bill expense income inflow commitment dates paid

articles.title: Set savings goals and finance preferences
articles.summary: Track a named savings objective and configure financial assumptions.
articles.before: Decide the target amount and how actual progress will be recorded.
steps: In TARGETS, review Active Saving Goals. Enter Goal name and Target amount under Initialise new objective.
Choose ACTIVATE GOAL MATRIX after reviewing the objective. Confirm the saved goal and its progress.
In CORE, review opening cash ledger, spending thresholds and the finance currency labels.
Check the saved result after any change. Compare starting balances with real records so targets and dashboards begin from supported data.
articles.check: The goal has a clear amount and the baseline supports the financial view.
articles.note: Goal progress is a record in FFPRO; it is not proof that money is held in a separate bank account. Keep the goal’s recorded progress aligned with the evidence of actual savings.
articles.tags: savings goal target preferences currency opening cash thresholds

articles.title: Use projects, calendars and scenario forecasts
articles.summary: Connect tasks and commitments with a realistic planning scenario.
articles.before: Keep project and calendar information current. Treat future returns and contributions as assumptions.
steps: Open Projects to review active plans, closed projects and the Idea Bin. Use Start new project or Start planning for an intended new plan.
Open Calendar to inspect dates, the day’s operational agenda and available Google Meet links. Check times on the source event.
Open Forecast and adjust Time horizon, Monthly contribution and Expected ROI only for a deliberate scenario.
Read the forecast as an estimate. Compare the contribution with Available surplus and reconcile contradictory feedback before taking action.
articles.check: The scenario’s inputs and resulting projection are understood. A projected milestone is not a guaranteed outcome.
articles.note: If forecast feedback conflicts with available surplus, review the underlying cash flow and commitments. Scenario returns are assumptions, not guaranteed outcomes.
articles.tags: forecast roi investment return surplus projects calendar scenario

articles.title: Check gateways and funding sources
articles.summary: Understand which data connections are real, manual or unavailable.
articles.before: Use the approved integration settings and your own authorised credentials.
steps: In GATEWAYS, read the connection type and status for each bank or investment portal. A MANUAL label does not establish live bank synchronisation.
Read the Google Workspace gateway scope. The documented Calendar integration is one-way and read-only from Google into FFPRO.
Check local AI status and configuration. Read any cloud-fallback settings before processing sensitive information.
In Funding, choose a status filter and sort order. Verify each opportunity’s eligibility, deadline and original source.
articles.check: Connection claims match the displayed scope and the data can be traced to its source.
articles.note: If funding cannot load, retry when available or contact support. A load error does not prove there are no opportunities.
articles.tags: gateway bank banking linked manual sync ollama ai funding opportunities load integration

articles.title: Create a project plan and manage its lifecycle
articles.summary: Organise a project under an appropriate planning type.
articles.before: Decide the project’s purpose, title and initial scope before creating it.
steps: Select Start new project and choose Standard Event, Vacation / Trip Plan or Startup Planner.
Enter Plan title / Project designation. Check the selected type and the final action label before submitting the new plan.
Open the saved plan from Active Projects and review its phases, assets and checklist before using generated figures or documents.
Use Close project when archiving an ended plan and Reopen when resuming it. Use sharing controls only for collaborators who should access that plan.
articles.check: The saved title and planning type match the intended project. Existing projects remain separate from the Idea Bin.
articles.note: Startup Planner describes price modelling and 1/3/5-year P&L statements. Those outputs require review against the business’s real assumptions before a bank or funding submission.
articles.tags: create project startup event vacation trip plan close reopen share collaborator idea bin

articles.title: Use the calendar and source event links
articles.summary: Review meetings, project dates and the daily operational agenda.
articles.before: Confirm the correct month and the device timezone before interpreting event times.
steps: Use Previous month, Today and Next month to navigate the calendar.
Select a day and inspect Day Operational Agenda. Use + more View when the day contains additional events.
Open the source Google Calendar link for authoritative event details or Join Google Meet for the correct meeting.
Use Sync Google Calendar when a source change has not appeared, then compare the updated details with the source event.
articles.check: The event date, time, title and meeting link agree with the source calendar.
articles.note: The documented gateway is Google-to-app read-only synchronisation. A local schedule edit or removal does not establish that the original Google Calendar event changed.
articles.tags: calendar google meet meeting sync day agenda month timezone event

articles.title: Navigate the growth workspace
articles.summary: Choose the correct tool for creating content, following enquiries or checking performance.
articles.before: Confirm the business name and profile before generating content.
steps: Read workspace readiness, connected channels, scheduled content and verified audience as separate measures.
Use Create for One Idea to Campaign, Zero-Prompt Creator and Graphic Studio. Use Calendar for planned posts and delivery results.
Use Customers for the pipeline and reviews, Growth for analytics and planning, and Business for profile, memory and Brand Kit.
Follow Recommended next actions when they reflect a real gap in your workspace, such as an incomplete profile.
articles.check: The selected screen matches the task you intend to complete and the business is correct.
articles.note: Visible credits and an online engine label do not by themselves prove that every provider connection can publish. Check Social and the channel-specific readiness information.
articles.tags: navigate home workspace growth create customers business calendar

articles.title: Complete the business profile
articles.summary: Provide factual business information used by content and the public storefront.
articles.before: Have approved contact details, products, opening hours and brand assets ready.
steps: Review Core Business Details: name, URL slug, industry, address, phone, WhatsApp, email, website and business story.
Use Brand Colors & AI Voice to configure presentation. Review Opening Hours and Products & Services Catalog for the actual offer.
Check logo and cover URLs and use Preview Public Page to inspect the storefront before relying on it.
Choose Save Profile, then reopen the saved fields and preview the page again.
articles.check: Saved information and the preview agree, especially phone numbers, website, opening hours and offers.
articles.note: Treat the public profile as customer-facing. Changing a URL slug can affect links you already distribute. Do not describe an unconfirmed service, price or guarantee as part of the business profile.
articles.tags: profile opening hours phone whatsapp website email public storefront contact save business logo slug

articles.title: Maintain business memory and Brand Kit
articles.route: Marketing > Business > Business Memory; Brand Kit
articles.summary: Store reusable facts, voice and audience context for more consistent output.
articles.before: Separate verified business facts from creative preferences and untested claims.
steps: In Business Memory, review Brand Core & Voice and the Primary description, voice, colours and preferred posting times.
Review Products & Services, Audience & Goals, Stored FAQs and Campaign Learnings & Memory. Keep facts specific and current.
Select Save Brain after reviewing edits. Auto-Optimize Knowledge displays a credit charge; inspect the proposed effect before using it.
Open Brand Kit to review palette, typography and logo. Use its style-guide download when the saved identity is correct.
articles.check: The saved memory describes the intended business and the Brand Kit matches its approved identity.
articles.note: The manual documents Business Memory and Brand Kit. It does not verify a My marketing skill editor; use the actual navigation or contact support.
articles.tags: memory brand kit colours voice audience faq marketing skill save brain

articles.title: Build a campaign plan from one idea
articles.route: Marketing > Create > One Idea to Campaign
articles.summary: Turn a confirmed offer into a reviewable campaign plan.
articles.before: Know the offer, audience and next action you want customers to take.
steps: Complete “What are you promoting?”, “Who needs it?” and “What should they do next?”.
Expand Add confirmed offer details when you have a verified price, discount or other terms to include.
Choose Build campaign plan. Review the proposed audience, claims, steps and calls to action against the information you supplied.
Choose Save campaign plan only when it is accurate. Find it under Growth > 30-Day Growth Plans and prepare individual content from the reviewed plan.
articles.check: The saved plan reflects the business’s real offer and a clear next step for the audience.
articles.note: This screen creates a plan only. Nothing is published or scheduled here. Example: promote managed ICT support to small Caribbean businesses and invite them to request a service review; do not invent a discount.
articles.tags: campaign plan idea promote offer audience cta save growth

articles.title: Create channel copy and choose destinations
articles.summary: Prepare a post for specific channels using verified offer details.
articles.before: Complete the business profile and confirm the offer. Have an approved media URL if the chosen channel needs it.
steps: Choose a promotion type, then fill Promotion / Product Title, Verified Details / Offer and Extra direction.
Choose Generate Channel Copy. Review each platform preview, including factual claims, spelling, media and the call to action.
Select exactly the intended publishing channels. Read each connection status and media requirement.
Enter Public HTTPS media URL where required and review Schedule date & time. Check the browser/device timezone against Saint Lucia time before scheduling.
articles.check: Every selected channel has reviewed copy and the required media. The date/time corresponds to the intended Saint Lucia schedule.
articles.note: Instagram and TikTok require a public HTTPS media URL; TikTok also needs the URL/domain verified in its developer console. The visible WhatsApp preview is labelled Copy Only.
articles.tags: post copy content generate channel instagram tiktok whatsapp media url domain preview

articles.title: Schedule content and verify provider delivery
articles.summary: Follow a scheduled item through the provider’s actual delivery result.
articles.before: Approve the exact post, media, channels and schedule first. Check current provider readiness.
steps: From Create & Schedule a Post, review the final selection and use Schedule Selected Channels for the intended post.
Return to Calendar. Use the channel filters and month navigation to find the saved item.
Read Provider delivery status for each destination. A queued or waiting item is still pending delivery.
After the scheduled time, inspect each provider result and verify the public post where appropriate. Investigate failed or attention-required deliveries before retrying.
articles.check: A published result is supported by a separate provider delivery record for that channel.
articles.note: Check providers separately. One channel’s success or failure does not establish the result for the other destinations.
articles.tags: schedule publish calendar delivery status queue pending failed timezone post

articles.title: Connect a social account and review readiness
articles.summary: Make sure the intended business account is authorised to publish.
articles.before: You need administrator rights on the relevant provider account and approved application credentials.
steps: Open Social Media Connections and inspect current accounts, last verification and token-expiry information.
Choose Connect New Account for the intended provider. Complete the provider’s official authorisation flow with the correct business account.
Return to Marketing and verify the account identity and available publishing readiness.
Prepare a reviewed post and check the delivery result before treating the connection as operational.
articles.check: The right provider account is listed and its required permissions and credentials are current.
articles.note: A Connected label alone does not prove publishing readiness. Verify the intended account, permissions, credentials and token expiry.
articles.tags: connect facebook instagram youtube tiktok social account oauth credentials token expired permissions ready

articles.title: Capture customer enquiries and attribution
articles.route: Marketing > Customers > Customer Pipeline > Add New Customer Inquiry
articles.summary: Keep enquiries and their evidenced source in a manageable pipeline.
articles.before: Confirm the customer details and how they found the business.
steps: Enter Customer Full Name and Phone / WhatsApp Number.
Choose Channel Source: WhatsApp Direct, Facebook Page Message, Google Business Profile or Website Form.
Choose a Related marketing campaign only when the customer reported it or reliable evidence supports it. Otherwise retain Unknown or no campaign.
Select Save Inquiry, then find the record in the pipeline and review its follow-up stage.
articles.check: The saved enquiry has accurate contact details and a justified source. Pipeline stages include New Inquiries, Interested, Follow Up Needed, Customers and VIP Repeat.
articles.note: This is manual attribution, not verified ad-click tracking. Do not assign every enquiry to the latest campaign just to improve a campaign’s reported performance.
articles.tags: customer inquiry enquiry crm pipeline attribution campaign source lead contact follow up

articles.title: Read reviews, analytics and planning drafts
articles.summary: Use verified results to decide what to improve next.
articles.before: Check the relevant reporting period and provider connection before interpreting results.
steps: In Review Management, use the sentiment filters and inspect actual reviews from connected sources.
In Simple Analytics, select Last 7d, Last 30d or Last 90d and inspect reach, impressions, engagement and clicks.
Use Market Benchmarks only with public competitor evidence. Its regional audit displays a credit charge; review before starting it.
Use Internal Agent Drafts to save a Title and Planning brief with Save internal draft only. Review the saved draft before converting it into any live campaign.
articles.check: Your decision is supported by provider data or clearly labelled internal planning information.
articles.note: Drafts and queued posts do not produce verified reach. Internal drafts cannot send, schedule, publish or charge customers. Check Brand Kit separately for visual consistency.
articles.tags: analytics review reach impressions engagement clicks benchmarks draft internal

articles.title: Create a branded graphic
articles.summary: Prepare an image layout in the format required by its destination.
articles.before: Check the business profile, logo, colours and confirmed offer first.
steps: Enter Prompt & Visual Description with the exact message and factual offer details.
Choose the required format: Instagram Square 1080 × 1080, Story / Reel / TikTok 1080 × 1920, Facebook Cover 1200 × 630 or LinkedIn Banner 1200 × 627.
Choose Visual Style Preset, then Generate Branded Graphic when the inputs are ready.
Inspect Canvas Preview for spelling, price, phone number, logo and cropping. Use Download Image or Save to Asset Library only after the result is correct.
articles.check: The downloaded or saved image matches the chosen dimensions and approved brand information.
articles.note: The format names above reproduce the app’s current labels and sizes. A graphic’s creation or download does not schedule or publish it. Confirm current provider requirements before using an asset in a post.
articles.tags: graphic image design generate download asset logo format dimensions

articles.title: Find the right course
articles.summary: Choose training by topic, level, access requirements and learning outcomes.
articles.before: You can browse the catalogue without a learner sign-in.
steps: Use Search courses and the Application, Level and Access filters. Clear filters if an expected course disappears.
Read each course card’s description, duration, lesson count and current access label.
Open the course title or View details. Review What you’ll learn, Before you begin and Course outline.
Choose Start free, View access or Start learning according to the current course access. Sign in with the separate Academy account when prompted.
articles.check: The selected course’s requirements and outcomes fit the learner’s needs.
articles.note: A displayed price does not establish that checkout is live or that access has been granted. Follow the course’s current access control.
articles.tags: course search training learn catalogue enrol enrollment price free paid access

articles.title: Create a learner account or sign in
articles.route: Academy > Sign in or Start learning
articles.summary: Save course access and progress under the correct learner identity.
articles.before: Academy uses its own learner account. Hub sign-in does not automatically establish that learner session.
steps: For an existing account, choose Already registered? Sign in if the registration form is shown.
Enter the learner’s email and password in the sign-in form. For a new account, use the account-creation form with Full name, Email and a password meeting the displayed requirement.
After sign-in, confirm the learner identity and return to the intended course.
If the password is rejected, use the recovery direction on screen: contact the Academy administrator for a reset. Do not create a duplicate learner to recover old progress.
articles.check: The Academy itself shows a signed-in learner state before you expect enrolment or progress to persist.
articles.note: Academy uses a separate learner account. The manual does not verify authenticated lesson-player controls. Never provide your password in help chat.
articles.tags: academy login register account password reset sign in learner access

articles.title: Plan course study and confirm progress
articles.summary: Use the published outline to prepare study and practical evidence.
articles.before: Review access and sign in with the learner who will complete the work.
steps: Read the course prerequisites and outline, then choose Start learning when the account has access.
Work through the lesson content and practical activities in the order required by that course.
Use the actual completion and assessment controls shown in the learner workspace. Return to the course to confirm what it recorded.
If progress, assessment access or a certificate is missing, provide the administrator with the course, lesson and a non-sensitive screenshot of the issue.
articles.check: Progress should be confirmed inside the learner’s account. A public course page or Hub percentage alone does not prove lesson or assessment completion.
articles.note: The manual does not verify exact authenticated lesson, assessment or certificate controls. For missing progress or certificates, contact the Academy administrator with the course and lesson, without sharing passwords.
articles.tags: lesson progress completion certificate assessment quiz course learning

articles.title: Choose a mission package
articles.route: Hub > My Apps > CombatZone SLU > Enter the Zone
articles.summary: Prepare a booking request for the appropriate occasion and play window.
articles.before: Know the approximate group size, occasion, preferred area and date.
steps: Choose Explore Packages for public, birthday or event options, or Request a Mission for corporate and resort operations.
Read the selected package’s included players, base play time, price, minimum charge and any deposit or extra-player terms.
Select the intended mission and continue to team configuration.
Check whether your group requires rotations or a custom arrangement before proceeding to date and location.
articles.check: The selected mission matches the occasion and the price basis you intend to request.
articles.note: The booking page states that availability, travel outside the Gros Islet/Castries core, venue requirements and custom arrangements need team confirmation. No online payment is taken in this request flow.
articles.tags: laser tag booking package mission price deposit corporate birthday event group

articles.title: Configure teams and plan the deployment
articles.summary: Check group capacity, rotations and the proposed event window.
articles.before: Select the intended mission package first.
steps: Set the player count with the plus/minus controls or quick choices. Review the balanced team map.
Check current simultaneous capacity, team sizes and rotation information on the booking page.
Choose Set Deployment. Select the preferred date, available start window and location type.
Enter Town / Area and Venue / Address. Review time, location, travel and venue conditions.
articles.check: The plan separates purchased play time from setup/turnaround and explains how the group will rotate.
articles.note: Rotations stay inside the purchased play window. Setup and scheduling buffers are not extra play time. Safety decisions override weather preference.
articles.tags: players teams capacity rotation deployment date time venue location

articles.title: Review a booking request before submission
articles.route: CombatZone booking > Deployment > Registration > Operator > Confirm
articles.summary: Prepare complete details for the team to review and confirm.
articles.before: Use actual customer details only when you intend to submit a booking request.
steps: Complete the required date, start window, location type, town and venue fields.
Continue through the registration and operator stages using the instructions displayed for the selected mission.
On Confirm, review the full package, group size, date, time, venue, contact details and commercial terms before submitting.
Keep the request reference or acknowledgement. Wait for the CombatZone team’s confirmation of availability and arrangements before treating the event as booked.
articles.check: The customer has a submitted request and later confirmation, rather than assuming that choosing a time reserved the slot.
articles.note: The manual does not verify final registration/operator fields or the submission receipt. Follow the live form and wait for team confirmation before treating the event as booked.
articles.tags: booking request confirm submit registration operator acknowledgement reference availability
